text:
sara_cs: Hey team — ACME reported intermittent 500s from our /v1/generate route but they say no request id shows up in their dashboard. Need the minimal handoff checklist so support can ask the customer and escalate if we need logs.

mike_oncall: Quick checklist I use: 1) exact timestamp(s) (UTC) 2) full response headers from one failed call 3) a minimal curl that reproduces the error (if possible) 4) debug token from the Console or SDK logs / HAR.

oliver_research: Add these specifics to the ask: status code, response body (or snippet), model name, route, and approximate latency. Also tell them to NOT paste API keys — only include header names + values we need: e.g., x-redwood-request-id: abc123 (we only need the id).

mike_oncall: Example curl to give the customer — ask them to run and paste output (response headers + body):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```

Then tell them to copy the `x-redwood-request-id` value from the response headers. If nothing shows, have them run with verbose to capture wire: `curl --verbose ...` and paste the full terminal output.

sara_cs: How do we ask them to get a debug token from Console? Some customers don't know where to look.

mike_oncall: Console steps: Open Console -> Requests -> find the time window -> click the request -> click "Copy debug token" (or "Export debug bundle"). If Console is down for them, ask for a HAR export from the browser. Steps: DevTools -> Network -> reproduce -> right-click -> Save all as HAR with content.

oliver_research: SDK mobile snippet if they use our SDKs: ask them to enable request-id logging:

- JavaScript SDK: `Redwood.config({ debug: true })` or set `window.__REDWOOD_DEBUG__ = true` before initializing.
- Android: enable verbose SDK logs (Logcat) and look for `x-redwood-request-id` lines.
- iOS: enable SDK debug logs (os_log) and grep for `request-id`

Also mention the small header name we use so they can grep: `x-redwood-request-id` (case-insensitive).

mike_oncall: If they can share a HAR or debug bundle, ask them to attach it to the support ticket and include: 
- exact UTC timestamps (start-end)
- the failing endpoint + model
- a minimal curl reproducer (copy/paste)
- the `x-redwood-request-id` if present
- redwood SDK version (if using SDK)

sara_cs: Anything about redaction or PII?

oliver_research: Yes — always instruct them to redact API keys, personal user data, and any internal IDs. It's fine for them to redact bearer tokens but leave the request-id values intact. If they accidentally paste keys, tell them to rotate the key immediately and let us know.

mike_oncall: If customer reports high latency but still gets success responses, ask for: median p50/p95 latencies, a sample request payload, and the `x-redwood-request-id` for a few example calls so we can trace on our side.

sara_cs: Cool. I'll paste this into the ticket template. Anything else?

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Checklist template applied to ticket #12345 by sara_cs

oliver_research: One final pro tip: if they can't reproduce, ask them to run a background capture for a window (e.g., 10 minutes) and then share the timestamps. That usually catches intermittent 500s.

mike_oncall: TL;DR to paste into customer message: "Please send (1) one curl run (`curl -i ...`) showing response headers, (2) the x-redwood-request-id header value from that response (or verbose curl output), (3) a debug token or HAR export from the Console/DevTools or SDK logs, (4) exact UTC timestamps and the minimal payload that causes the error. Redact API keys and any PII. Attach everything to this ticket and we'll pick it up for deeper traces."

sara_cs: Perfect — thanks everyone :pray:
